sentences.text:
In order to prove the defence taken by the
respondent no.2 they have examined the Branch
Manager of Esi, Bommasandra as Rw.1 and through
him Ex.R1 and R2 are marked.

Ex.R1 is the letter
addressed to the court by the Branch Manager Esic,
Bommasandra to the effect that the said office has not
made any kind of Esi cash benefit to the petitioner.

The
Rw1 has produced even Nil ledger sheets.

The Rw.1
has deposed that as per records they have not given Esi
benefit to the petitioner.

18 . In the judgment relied by the learned counsel
for respondent no.2, referring Sec.53 and 61 of the
Employees State Insurance Act it was held that "the
petition under the Workmen's Compensation Act or the
Employees Compensation Act is barred and the victim
has to approach the Esi Corporation for compensation.

In the said case, the victim had applied for Esi facilities
and code was allotted to the victim.

The subscription to
the Esi facility was categorically stated by respondent
no.1 and 2 in their written statement.

The said fact was
not denied by the petitioner.

However they contended
that they have not availed the compensation under the
Esi Act.

In the above referred case, the Hon'ble High
 Scch-24 10 Mvc 6930/2022
 c/w
 6931/2022
Court has made reference of several judgment rendered
by Hon'ble High Court and Supreme Court.

In all the
cases specific observation was made with reference to
the word "Employment Injury suffered by the victim .

It
means Sec. 53 and 61 of Esi Act would apply only to
the Employment Injury suffered by the victim during the
course of employment.
 19.

In the present case, the petitioner has not
suffered injury during the course of Employment.

It is
nowhere the case that the petitioner has suffered injury
during the course of employment.

The present petition
is not filed under Eca.

Hence, the observation made in
the aforesaid ruling has no application to the case in
hand.

Hence, the claim petition filed by the petitioner is
Chandra Kumar.R vs Subramani on 1 October, 2024

Hence additional issue in Mvc

and M.V.C.No.6931/2022

P.W.1 and Pw2 have given evidence to
the effect that at the time of accident P.W.1 as rider and
Pw.2 as pillion rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg
No.KA-44-V-4114 were proceeding on Gowrenahalli
village, Kasaba Hobli, Anekal Taluk, at that time, the
driver of Tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-03-T-0490
(hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) came
from opposite direction at very high speed, in a rash and
negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's vehicle
and caused the accident.
 21.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash
and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, the P.W.1
and Pw.2 have relied upon Ex.P1 to P7 which are the
police records such as F.I.R with complaint, spot
mahazar, seizure mahazar, wound certificate, Imv
report, notice u/Sec.133 of Imv Act, statement of
accused and charge sheet etc.,
 22.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by
petitioner/Chandra Kumar in Mvc No.6930/2022, case
has been registered against the driver of offending

 6931/2022
vehicle in Crime No 0237/2022 of Anekal Police Station
for the offence punishable under section 279, 337 of Mv
Act.

The Investigation officer after investigation filed
charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for
the offence punishable under Section 279, 337, 338 of
Ipc.
 23.

The respondents No.2 has seriously disputed
the manner of accident one stated by the petitioners
and submitted that rash and negligent driving of the
Chandra Kumar.R vs Subramani on 1 October, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186173145/
7

two wheeler by the Pw1 itself is the sole cause for
accident.

Hence the liability to pay compensation may
be fixed on the owner and insurer of the motorcycle.

24 . Though the petitioners in both the petition
have categorically contended that the driver of the
offending vehicle alone has contributed negligence and
though the investigation officer after investigation has
filed charge sheet only against the driver of the
offending vehicle, but if the materials placed on record
is perused, at the time of accident the petitioners were
proceeding from Anekal towards Jigani and offending
vehicle was coming from opposite direction i.e., from
Jigani towards Anekal.

Though the Pw.1 and Pw.2 have
 Scch-24 13 Mvc 6930/2022
 c/w
 6931/2022
deposed that the said road is one way road and the
offending vehicle which came from wrong direction hit
against their vehicle but if the spot mahazar is perused,
wherein it is mentioned that it is two way roads.

As it is
a two way road there is provision to ply vehicles on both
direction of the road.

The width of the as per Ex.P2 is 20
feet and the accident in question has occurred in the
middle of the road.

When petitioners were proceeding
from Anekal towards Jigani they ought to have ridden
their vehicle on the left side of the road and when the
driver of the offending vehicle was proceeding from
Jigani towards Anekal he ought to have driven his
vehicle on the left side of the said road.

But the Pw.1
and the driver of offending vehicle by riding/driving
their respective vehicle in the middle of the road

have
contributed equal amount of negligence.

It is relevant to
state here that the petitioners have not produced eye
sketch before the court.

It appears that intentionally the
petitioners have suppressed the sketch before the court.
Hence, merely because the investigation officer has filed
charge sheet only against the driver of the offending
vehicle the court cannot on the basis of police document
arrive at the conclusion that the driver of the offending
vehicle alone is responsible for the accident.

As
 Scch-24 14 Mvc 6930/2022
 c/w
 6931/2022
petitioner in Mvc No.6930/2022 has contributed
negligence to the extent of 50% he has to forgo
compensation to the extent of 50%.

Further though
petitioner in Mvc No.6931/2022 is the pillion rider in
Chandra Kumar.R vs Subramani on 1 October, 2024

the two wheeler but he has failed to array the owner and
insurer of the motorcycle in which he was riding hence
he is also to forgo compensation to the extent of 50%.
Hence, Issue no.1 in both the cases is answered in
partly affirmative.
